description.text:
The Black Star Promos of the EX years, numbered 001 to 040 between 2003 and 2006. When Nintendo of America took over the game outside Japan from Wizards of the Coast, it began a new run of promos, with Pokémon USA creating and making the cards; Nintendo handled marketing and distribution until the end of 2005, when Pokémon USA took over.

Kyogre ex and Groudon ex opened the set through the Pokémon Ruby & Sapphire Challenge and Nintendo Power magazine. Players earned others in the e-League, which also gave jumbo winner copies, and at POP tournaments; collectors found them in EX Series tins, value packs and gift sets, Target's snack bar promotion, and the Pokémon Heroes and Jirachi: Wish Maker DVDs. The World Championships trophy cards Tropical Wind (2004), Tropical Tidal Wave (2005, 2006) and Championship Arena (2005) belong here too.

description.text: A holofoil version of Ken Sugimori's Mudkip from EX Ruby & Sapphire, with the Pokémon Organized Play logo, a Poké Ball, embossed in silver in the corner of the art. It was the first of three Hoenn starter prize cards, before Torchic and Treecko: UK tournament organizers received it in January 2004, the first promo to reach Europe before the United States. From June 2004 each sanctioned tournament in North America was sent a pack of four, one each for the top three players and the fourth for a player drawn at random.

sources.title: Pokumon: Top Sixteen Tropical Wind (026/Nintendo Black Star English Promo)
PkmnCards: Tropical Wind · Nintendo Black Star Promos #026

description.text:
Tropical Wind was the promo card of the 2004 Pokémon World Championships, held from 20 to 22 August 2004 at the Wyndham Palace Resort & Spa at Walt Disney World, near Orlando, Florida, where Japanese players won all three age groups. Each competitor received nine cards: the card in seven languages, each with a "Worlds 04" stamp, plus two insert cards. Collectors say plain unstamped copies went to spectators in far larger numbers.

The trophy versions carry a placement stamp instead: Top Sixteen, Quarter-Finalist, Semi-Finalist and, highest, Finalist. Unlike in later years, players received only the card for their best placement, so the 2004 trophy cards are scarcer than those that followed. Staff running the event got a Staff copy.

sources.title: Pokumon: Championship Arena (028/Nintendo Black Star English Promo)

description.text: Championship Arena was a surprise gift for competitors at the 2005 Pokémon World Championships, held from 19 to 21 August 2005 at the Town and Country Resort and Convention Center in San Diego. It was slipped under the doors of their hotel rooms in a folded pamphlet, so unevenly that some got duplicates and others none. Spectators got no card that year, unlike 2004, when they were given an unstamped Tropical Wind 026. Two months later the same art, Ryo Ueda's arena with Mew and Celebi on its screen, became Battle Road Stadium, promo 117/PCG-P, in Japan: the prize at Battle Road Autumn 2005 (23 October to 3 November 2005), whose new six-stage tournament was also called the Battle Road Stadium, for players who beat the Pokémon Card Laboratory researcher at the sixth and last stage. Players who reached the final tournament of Battle Road Spring 2006 got it too.

PkmnCards: Groudon ex · Nintendo Black Star Promos #038

description.text: The holofoil Groudon ex from the Groudon tin, one of three EX Collector's Tins released in October 2006 with Kyogre, Groudon or Rayquaza on the lid. Each held four booster packs, two of EX Crystal Guardians and two of EX Emerald, and the ex of the Pokémon on its tin. Ryo Ueda's three ex cards began in Japan as Players Club promos, Groudon ex as 028/PLAY, in the Limited Edition Starter Kit that club members could order by mail or buy at some official tournaments during the 2005 season.
